tone: warm, personal, commendatory, hopeful, and pastoral
target_reader: religion-naive adults and older adolescents near grade 6
translation_identity: firmly dynamic-equivalence, NLT-like in readability but independent

sealed_unit.instruction: The completed human-edited wording of Philippians 2:1-18 is excluded from blind drafting. Preserve only the source-text discourse transition into verse 19.

governing_rules: The prose serves the reader; the apparatus serves accountability.
Translate meaning, logic, tone, discourse movement, and theological force rather than Greek surface form.
Use clear natural oral English; reorder, split, unpack, and clarify implied relationships when comprehension benefits.
Preserve the paragraph’s movement from Paul’s hope to send Timothy, through Timothy’s proven character and sincere concern, to Paul’s hope of coming personally.
Do not turn idioms or relational images into unsupported commentary; document consequential resolutions as risks or human questions.
No comparison translations, traditional benchmark wording, conversational drafts, or sealed human wording may enter blind drafting.
existing_decisions: Use Christ and Jesus Christ naturally according to the source reference.
Render εὐαγγέλιον as the good news when context permits.
Maintain the reader-first dynamic center established by the audited Philippians benchmark without exposing its wording to blind workers.

units.title: Paul hopes to send Timothy
known_issues: Verse 19’s hope is explicitly grounded 'in the Lord Jesus'; preserve dependence on the Lord without making the English stiff or formulaic.
Verse 19’s εὐψυχῶ means to be encouraged or cheered by receiving news about the Philippians; make the emotional result clear.
Verse 20’s ἰσόψυχον describes Timothy as like-minded or sharing Paul’s concern. Avoid implying absolute identity in every respect.
Verse 20’s μεριμνήσει is positive, sincere care for their welfare, despite the word family’s possible association with anxiety elsewhere.

Verse 21 contrasts self-interest with the interests or cause of Jesus Christ. Identify the contrast naturally without exaggerating Paul’s statement into a universal condemnation of every Christian worker.
Verse 22’s δοκιμή refers to Timothy’s tested and proven character, which the Philippians already know.

Verse 22 uses a father-child image for Timothy serving with Paul in advancing the good news. Preserve both their close relationship and Timothy’s active partnership; avoid making him sound merely subordinate or childish.
Verse 23 says Paul will send Timothy as soon as Paul sees how his own circumstances turn out. Make the referent clear without inventing details.
Verse 24 again grounds Paul’s confidence in the Lord and expresses hope that Paul himself will come soon.

verses.greek: Ἐλπίζω δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Τιμόθεον ταχέως πέμψαι ὑμῖν ἵνα κἀγὼ εὐψυχῶ γνοὺς τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν
οὐδένα γὰρ ἔχω ἰσόψυχον ὅστις γνησίως τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν μεριμνήσει
οἱ πάντες γὰρ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ζητοῦσιν οὐ τὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
τὴν δὲ δοκιμὴν αὐτοῦ γινώσκετε ὅτι ὡς πατρὶ τέκνον σὺν ἐμοὶ ἐδούλευσεν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον
τοῦτον μὲν οὖν ἐλπίζω πέμψαι ὡς ἂν ἀφίδω τὰ περὶ ἐμὲ ἐξαυτῆς
πέποιθα δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι καὶ αὐτὸς ταχέως ἐλεύσομαι
